pr_body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Fixes some of the issues seen in #31604

Restarting a remote ser2net service triggers the error below. OSError is thrown after which the dsmr component stops updating. This pull requests improves retry logic of the dsmr component by handling OSError accordingly.

Error log
```
ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/dsmr/sensor.py", line 143, in connect_and_reconnect
    transport, protocol = await hass.loop.create_task(reader_factory())
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 1025, in create_connection
    raise exceptions[0]
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 1010, in create_connection
    sock = await self._connect_sock(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 924, in _connect_sock
    await self.sock_connect(sock, address)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/selector_events.py", line 494, in sock_connect
    return await fut
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/selector_events.py", line 526, in _sock_connect_cb
    raise OSError(err, f'Connect call failed {address}')
OSError: [Errno 113] Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 2001)
```

issue_context.title: DSMR component does not always reconnect with ser2net failures
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem

The [DSMR Slimme Meter](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/dsmr/) component will not always reconnect when using ser2net. I mostly experience this issue when my internet router restarts.

## Environment

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 104.0 and higher
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): n/a
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Hass.io
- Integration causing this issue: DSMR Slimme Meter
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/dsmr/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`

```yaml
- platform: dsmr
  host: 192.168.1.25
  port: 8088
  dsmr_version: 4
```

## Traceback/Error logs

n/a

## Additional information

I suspect that [this piece of code](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/dsmr/sensor.py#L137-L148) is the main culprit:

```python
# Start DSMR asyncio.Protocol reader
try:
    transport, protocol = await hass.loop.create_task(reader_factory())
except (
    serial.serialutil.SerialException,
    ConnectionRefusedError,
    TimeoutError,
):
    # Log any error while establishing connection and drop to retry
    # connection wait
    _LOGGER.exception("Error connecting to DSMR")
    transport = None
```

Perhaps the correct `Exception` / `Error` isn't caught by the except handler, thus the code exiting out of the loop. Unfortunately I could not find any logging related to this issue, so I cannot be sure.
comments:
Same problem,

SER2NET restart is not the fix.

running hassio on a QNAP nas. when the nas awakes after sleeping the vm is resumed. after this the last values are shown. only on hassio restart the meter works again.

It seems like a TimeoutError error is caught which is the builtin Python TimeoutError. When creating a TCP task it's done with asyncio in the dsmr_parser library which can throw an asyncio.TimeoutError.

I'm updating the DSMR integration to work with UI configuration, I'll add the asyncio.TimeoutError and you can try if that solves your problem.

Seems that restarting a server on which ser2net is running will cause an OSError that is not handled correctly.

```ERROR (MainThread) [homeassistant] Error doing job: Task exception was never retrieved
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/components/dsmr/sensor.py", line 143, in connect_and_reconnect
    transport, protocol = await hass.loop.create_task(reader_factory())
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 1025, in create_connection
    raise exceptions[0]
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 1010, in create_connection
    sock = await self._connect_sock(
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/base_events.py", line 924, in _connect_sock
    await self.sock_connect(sock, address)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/selector_events.py", line 494, in sock_connect
    return await fut
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.8/asyncio/selector_events.py", line 526, in _sock_connect_cb
    raise OSError(err, f'Connect call failed {address}')
OSError: [Errno 113] Connect call failed ('127.0.0.1', 2001)
```

Changing the code to catch OSError does fix the issues that I am experiencing (https://github.com/jwnmulder/core/commit/897f9d7c809ffa929812992faac228a8ae59a261). I'm not sure if this is the right way to fix the retry handling?
Seems like the `OSError` is thrown when socket connect fails, so this needs to be added to the `except` clause.
Just created a pull request for handling OSError. Tested it a while on my side and seems to be working nicely

review_comments: I would keep the ConnectionRefusedError and TimeoutError, it seems both can be thrown by the supporting library so just adding OSError would suffice.
I'll add them back for documentation purpose then. Both are subclasses of OSError so functionality wise it is not really needed https://docs.python.org/3/library/exceptions.html#exception-hierarchy
If OSError covers them it's fine. Note that I added in another PR (#37464) the asyncio.TimeoutError, which seems to be different from TimeoutError.
Yeah I noticed that one too. I did not include it in this PR to avoid duplicate changes
